title: Dissimilarity-Based Markov Decision Processes for Stabilizing State Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2610.29024v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning for stochastic systems typically optimizes expected cumulative rewards, while reliable and repeatable behavior also depends on how the state distribution evolves over time. Optimizing expected return alone does not guarantee that this distribution converges to a desired target or remains stable. This paper develops a theoretical framework for learning policies that stabilize state distributions. We formulate the problem as a Dissimilarity-based Markov Decision Process (DMDP), in which the policy acts on the current state distribution and the objective measures its dissimilarity to a target distribution. We establish sufficient conditions under which the optimal policy makes the target distribution asymptotically stable. To support policy learning, we introduce a finite-dimensional representation of distributions and show how stability guarantees for its parameter dynamics extend to the underlying state distribution

translated_title: 用于稳定状态分布的基于相异度的马尔可夫决策过程
translated_abstract: 针对随机系统的强化学习通常优化期望累积奖励，然而可靠且可重复的行为还取决于状态分布随时间的演化方式。仅优化期望回报并不能保证该分布收敛到期望的目标分布或保持稳定。本文开发了一个用于学习能够稳定状态分布的策略的理论框架。我们将该问题表述为基于相异度的马尔可夫决策过程（DMDP），其中策略作用于当前状态分布，目标函数衡量其与目标分布的相异度。我们建立了充分条件，在这些条件下最优策略能使目标分布渐近稳定。为支持策略学习，我们引入了分布的有限维表示，并展示了其参数动力学的稳定性保证如何扩展到底层的状态分布。
tldr: 本文提出基于相异度的马尔可夫决策过程（DMDP）理论框架，其中策略作用于状态分布并通过最小化与目标分布的相异度进行优化，建立了最优策略使目标分布渐近稳定的充分条件，并通过分布的有限维表示将稳定性保证扩展到底层状态分布。
